title: Non-Hermitian Quantum Mechanics I: Instantaneous Self-Energy
authors: Lingfeng Liu, Wei-Wei Yang, Jiangping Hu, Zhesen Yang
abstract: Starting from the unitary evolution of a closed quantum system, we rigorously demonstrate that the projection of the global wavefunction onto an arbitrary local subsystem is governed by an exact, time-dependent non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation. Crucially, the derivation does not rely on conventional approximations such as the Born approximation, the Markov approximation, or the wide-band limit. The central quantity is the \textit{instantaneous self-energy}, a time-dependent and generally non-Hermitian operator that encodes environmental backaction and, together with the subsystem Hamiltonian, forms the exact time-local generator of the projected dynamics. By benchmarking the conventional non-Hermitian approximation against this exact framework, we systematically expose its limitations. These results provide a rigorous microscopic foundation for the emergence of effective non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum systems.
summary: This paper rigorously derives the effective non-Hermitian dynamics for a subsystem coupled to an environment, showing that the dynamics are governed by an exact, time-dependent self-energy. It achieves this without using standard approximations like the Born or Markov limits. The work establishes a fundamental, microscopic theory for how non-Hermiticity emerges in open quantum systems.
main_problem: To rigorously derive the effective non-Hermitian dynamics governing the projection of a global wavefunction onto a local subsystem without relying on conventional approximations.
main_result: The projected dynamics are governed by an exact, time-local non-Hermitian Schrödinger equation whose generator is determined by the instantaneous self-energy, $\Sigma_{	ext{inst}}(t)$.
method: The derivation uses the block-matrix form of the Schrödinger equation and projected propagators, providing an exact, self-consistent framework.
model_or_system: A closed single-particle quantum system partitioned into a subsystem ($S$) and an environment ($B$), described by a global Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$.
key_observables: Instantaneous self-energy ($\Sigma_{	ext{inst}}(t)$), probability flux ($\Gamma(t)$), and the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian $H_{	ext{eff}}(t)$.
important_parameters: Time-dependent operators, the global Hamiltonian $H$, and the initial state components in $S$ and $B$.
main_assumptions: The derivation is exact and holds over time intervals where the projected propagator $U_{SS}(t)$ remains invertible.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the microscopic origin of effective non-Hermitian dynamics via probability leakage from the local subsystem into the environment.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the exact time-local non-Hermitian generator using theorems derived from the block-matrix formalism, contrasts this with standard approximations (Born, Markov), and details the structure of the source term arising from initial environmental components.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, non-perturbative foundation for effective non-Hermitian dynamics, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems where approximations are often used.

(a) The wavefunction is initially local- ized within the subsystem. (b) Probability leaks out of the subsystem at early times, constituting the microscopic origin of effective non- Hermitian dynamics.

FIG. 2. 2 Benchmark of the NHA in the Anderson–Fano model. The decay rate Γ(t) = −2 Im[Σinst(t)] is plotted for a large environment (N = 4000, solid red line) and a small environment (N = 360, dashed blue line) alongside the constant on-shell FGR value ΓFGR (dashed black line) for model parameters tc = 5, V0 = 0.5, and λ = 0.7. The exact dynamics exhibits an initial buildup, an intermediate-time plateau that deviates from the FGR prediction, and persistent late-time non-Markovian oscillations. For the smaller environment, a pronounced recurrence spike interrupts the dynamics when the wave packet returns to the impurity after reflection from the boundary, at Trec ≈72.

FIG. 3. Quench-induced reconstruction of the instantaneous self-energy in the Anderson–Fano model. The impurity potential is changed from V0 = 0 to V1 = 4 at t1 = 10, with tc = 5 and λ = 0.7. Both Γ(t) = −2 Im Σinst(t) and ∆(t) = Re Σinst(t) remain continuous across the quench and then undergo transient relaxation toward their respective post-quench plateaus. The parenthetical labels (V0) and (V1) attached to ΓFGR and ∆FGR distinguish their values at the pre- and post-quench impurity potentials, respectively.
